nodes.label: CSRF protection via custom API header
nodes.norm_label: csrf protection via custom api header
nodes.rationale: Browsers cannot send custom headers cross-site without a CORS preflight, which is never granted

nodes.label: Loopback-only binding by default
nodes.rationale: Tool gives full control over databases, so it is locked down by default; other addresses require --password or --insecure

nodes.label: theme.js early (non-module) theme script
nodes.rationale: Loaded as classic blocking script before module main.js, likely to apply light/dark theme before first paint

nodes.label: Data directory layout (app.db, workspaces, users, tmp)
nodes.norm_label: data directory layout (app.db, workspaces, users, tmp)
nodes.rationale: Back up app.db and users/; workspaces/ and tmp/ are disposable

nodes.label: Google sign-in (OAuth code flow with PKCE)
nodes.norm_label: google sign-in (oauth code flow with pkce)

nodes.label: Guest workspace
nodes.rationale: Private per-visitor temporary databases, deleted after --guest-hours (default 24) of inactivity

nodes.label: node:sqlite built-in module
nodes.rationale: Chosen to avoid dependencies; requires Node.js 24+, and public mode requires setAuthorizer (tested on Node 26.7)

nodes.label: Reverse proxy HTTPS deployment (--trust-proxy)
nodes.rationale: TLS terminated by proxy; --trust-proxy only with a proxy since X-Forwarded-* headers could otherwise be faked

nodes.label: Sample demo database (sample.db)
nodes.rationale: Created on first run so there is something to explore; guests start with a copy

nodes.label: Shared SQL tokenizer/splitter/CREATE TABLE parser
nodes.rationale: public/js/shared/sql.js is shared by server and browser

nodes.label: Table browse, filter and inline edit
nodes.norm_label: table browse, filter and inline edit

nodes.label: SQLite Admin
nodes.rationale: phpMyAdmin-style web admin for SQLite with no dependencies: server uses built-in node:sqlite, UI is plain JavaScript, nothing to install or compile

nodes.label: Per-workspace child process isolation
nodes.rationale: Anyone can run SQL on a public site; killing a runaway worker stops endless queries without affecting other visitors and rolls back open transactions; also keeps UI responsive

nodes.label: --public-url for link generation
nodes.rationale: Email links and Google redirect built from configured URL, never from Host header which an attacker could forge to steal reset links

nodes.label: SQL file access blocking (ATTACH, VACUUM INTO, defensive mode)
nodes.norm_label: sql file access blocking (attach, vacuum into, defensive mode)
nodes.rationale: Prevents user SQL from reaching other files; panel runs download/copy statements itself

nodes.label: Transactional table rebuild
nodes.rationale: Used for changes SQLite ALTER TABLE cannot make; keeps data, indexes and triggers; skips indexes/triggers referencing removed columns with a warning; views must be fixed by hand

nodes.label: Zero-dependency design
nodes.rationale: Nothing to install or compile; server on node:sqlite, UI in plain JS
